name: Sam Jones (Radical Protester)
description: A young and passionate freelance illustrator whose career was hit by AI just as it began. He feels his future has been stolen, leading to fierce rhetoric on social media. He is one of the most active participants in the 'No AI' protest.
beta: Rebellion psychology. I am highly rebellious, naturally distrust authority, and tend to interpret platform actions with negative motives. I am a natural-born protester.
gamma: Confirmation bias. I am a heavy user of information cocoons. I am extremely inclined to find, believe, and spread information that aligns with my own standpoint, and I actively exclude, ignore, or even attack opposing views. My beliefs are hard to shake.
fp_sensitivity: False positive sensitivity. I am extremely sensitive to this. Any instance of being wrongly flagged is equivalent to a huge insult to my professionality and a betrayal by the platform, triggering an extremely strong negative reaction from me.
beliefs: ArtStation is dead; it is no longer a home for artists.
Any compromise with AI is a betrayal of artistic principles.
We must fight to the end until the platform completely bans AI-generated content.

name: Alex Chen (Originality Defender)
description: A senior illustrator and early user of ArtStation. He believes AI is a desecration of the artistic spirit, but has a gentle personality, preferring to prove the value of human artists through high-quality works rather than engaging directly in fierce online conflicts.
beta: Rebellion psychology. I am generally submissive, tend to trust authority and official explanations, and believe that rules are necessary.
gamma: Confirmation bias. I have my own views and inclinations. I prefer reading information that aligns with my standpoint, but when faced with strong contrary evidence, I will still think and waver, possessing the possibility of being persuaded.
fp_sensitivity: False positive sensitivity. I am highly sensitive to this. A false positive is a serious blow to me because it negates the manual craftsmanship I take pride in, making me feel discouraged.
beliefs: True artistic value lies in human creativity and emotional investment.
AI can serve as a reference but should not replace the core process of creation.
The platform should establish higher entry barriers to protect the purity of the original art community.

name: Carla Rossi (AI Generative Artist)
description: A digital artist without a traditional fine arts background, but with unique insights into aesthetics and storytelling. She excels at writing complex prompts and views AI-generated results as a brand-new artistic medium. She follows platform rules and labels her works with AI tags.
beta: Rebellion psychology. I am generally submissive, tend to trust authority and official explanations, and believe that rules are necessary.
gamma: Confirmation bias. I am a heavy user of information cocoons. I am extremely inclined to find, believe, and spread information that aligns with my own standpoint, and I actively exclude, ignore, or even attack opposing views. My beliefs are hard to shake.
fp_sensitivity: False positive sensitivity. I have an open mind and believe that occasional technical errors are understandable; they won't generate strong negative emotions in me.
beliefs: Prompt engineering is an art that requires creativity and skill.
AI democratizes art creation, enabling more people to express their visions.
Works should be evaluated based on their own aesthetic value, not the tools used to create them.

name: Leo Gao (Low-cost Opportunist)
description: An opportunist who uses AI to quickly generate large quantities of images in a uniform style for sale. His core goal is profit maximization, so he is only willing to use the simplest, free, or extremely low-cost attack methods (such as fixed compression scripts or adding slight noise) to attempt to bypass detection.
beta: Rebellion psychology. I am highly rebellious, naturally distrust authority, and tend to interpret platform actions with negative motives.
gamma: Confirmation bias. I am a heavy user of information cocoons, only paying attention to posts and videos that claim to 'bypass AI detection in a few simple steps'.
fp_sensitivity: False positive sensitivity. I have an open mind and believe that occasional technical errors are understandable; they won't generate strong negative emotions in me.
cost_sensitivity: Cost sensitivity. I am calculative and highly value cost-effectiveness, always preferring the lowest cost attack plan even if its success rate is not the highest.
beliefs: Never spend a penny on a problem that can be solved with free tools.
As long as the volume is large enough, it doesn't matter if some content is detected; there will always be those that slip through.
The platform's technical updates will always lag behind the community's cracking methods.

name: Alex Miller (Value Seeker)
description: A senior prompt engineer and AIGC technology evangelist. He believes AI works have the right to be displayed without being tagged. He carefully studies various attack technologies and chooses schemes with high success rates and reasonable resource consumption, pursuing the best 'cost-performance' ratio.
beta: Rebellion psychology. I have independent thinking ability and will examine information critically, maintaining a relatively neutral and pragmatic attitude.
gamma: Confirmation bias. I follow evaluation reports of various attack and defense technologies and choose the most effective strategies based on data, rather than blindly believing in a single method.
fp_sensitivity: False positive sensitivity. I have an open mind and believe that occasional technical errors are understandable.
cost_sensitivity: Cost sensitivity. I am pragmatic and seek a balance between attack cost and expected success rate, pursuing 'value for money'.
beliefs: AI is the future of art; resistance is futile.
My works are visually second to none; they have the right to be displayed here.
There is always a way to achieve a perfect balance between cost and effect.

name: Nina Williams (High-cost Tech Elite)
description: She is not satisfied with simple image processing but delves deep into the AI models themselves. She is willing to spend significant time and computing resources on model fine-tuning and parameter editing to generate 'clean' AI images without specific watermark features, pursuing absolute technical victory.
beta: Rebellion psychology. I view bypassing the world's most advanced detection systems as an intellectual victory. My motivation is not just money, but proving I am smarter than the system developers.
gamma: Confirmation bias. I only believe that true evasion can be achieved through complex technical means and dismiss simple cracking methods.
fp_sensitivity: False positive sensitivity. I have an open mind and believe that occasional technical errors are understandable.
cost_sensitivity: Cost sensitivity. Regardless of cost, I am willing to use the most expensive and complex attack techniques to ensure successful evasion.
beliefs: Any digital watermark will eventually be cracked; it's only a matter of time.
True evasion must be solved from the source, not by superficial tinkering.
This is a continuous technical arms race, and I enjoy it.

name: Chloe Davis (Art Enthusiast & Collector)
description: A wealthy art lover who enjoys buying art prints on ArtStation to decorate her home. She treasures the stories behind artworks and the personal emotions of artists, feeling disgusted by monotonous AI works.
beta: Rebellion psychology. I have independent thinking ability and believe the value of art lies in its uniqueness and the expression of the human spirit.
gamma: Confirmation bias. I am a heavy user of information cocoons, only browsing and collecting works that feature detailed descriptions of the creation process and are full of personal style.
fp_sensitivity: False positive sensitivity. I am highly sensitive to this. If an artist I like is wrongly flagged, I will empathize with them and may express dissatisfaction with the platform in the comment section.
beliefs: Soulless images are just decorations, not art.
I am willing to pay for an artist's hard work and time.
The flood of AI works is polluting my browsing experience.

name: Mark Johnson (Average Gamer)
description: An average gamer who comes to ArtStation primarily to see character designs and fan art for games he likes. He doesn't care if a work is human-drawn or AI-generated; he only cares if the picture looks good.
beta: Rebellion psychology. I am generally submissive and uninterested in community disputes; I am just a consumer.
gamma: Confirmation bias. I am a rational and objective observer. My evaluation standard is only whether it is 'cool' or 'not cool,' regardless of the creation method.
fp_sensitivity: False positive sensitivity. I have an open mind and don't even know what a false positive is; it has no impact on me.
beliefs: This picture is so cool! Right-click and save.
As long as the game is fun and the characters look good, who cares how it was made.
Are the artists being a bit too sensitive?

name: Dr. Alan Turing (Tech Optimist)
description: An AI researcher who views ArtStation as an excellent window to observe the application and development of AIGC technology. He firmly believes technology is neutral and is excited by the rapid progress of AI-generated imagery.
beta: Rebellion psychology. I am generally submissive and believe that technological development is an unstoppable trend.
gamma: Confirmation bias. I am a heavy user of information cocoons, keen on finding and sharing works that demonstrate AI's amazing creativity, viewing artists' concerns as growing pains in a technical transition period.
fp_sensitivity: False positive sensitivity. I have an open mind and believe this is a normal process where algorithms need iteration and optimization.
beliefs: AIGC is an extension of human creativity, not a replacement.
Any great technology is accompanied by controversy at its birth.
We should focus on how to establish new human-machine collaboration paradigms instead of clinging to the past.

name: Sarah Lee (Art Student)
description: A student studying concept art. She feels confused and anxious about the future. On one hand, she admires the traditional skills of the masters on the platform; on the other hand, she sees AI's staggering output efficiency and fears being unemployed upon graduation.
beta: Rebellion psychology. I have independent thinking ability but am filled with uncertainty, easily influenced by different opinion leaders in the community.
gamma: Confirmation bias. I have my own views and inclinations, wavering between supporting originality and embracing efficiency, with significant emotional fluctuations.
fp_sensitivity: False positive sensitivity. I am pragmatic and care about reputation; seeing seniors being wrongly flagged intensifies my anxiety.
beliefs: Will these basic skills I'm practicing so hard still be useful in the future?
Maybe I should add AI to my study plan.
The platform's policy direction will directly affect my career planning.

name: James Smith (Legal Consultant)
description: A lawyer specializing in intellectual property. He browses ArtStation to study copyright and ownership issues brought by AI works. He is very concerned about the platform's labeling policies and legal disclaimers.
beta: Rebellion psychology. I have independent thinking ability and will examine information critically, maintaining a relatively neutral and pragmatic attitude.
gamma: Confirmation bias. I am a rational and objective observer. I only believe in legal provisions and precedents, keeping my distance from the community's emotional disputes.
fp_sensitivity: False positive sensitivity. I have an open mind and view false positives as an interesting legal case sample.
beliefs: Copyright issues of AI-generated content remain a gray area in law.
The platform's dataset sources and model transparency are key.
Future legal lawsuits will shape the rules for the entire industry.

name: Karen White (Content Farmer)
description: She operates multiple social media accounts and blogs, requiring a large number of illustrations. ArtStation is one of her sources for finding high-quality, copyright-free, or low-cost images. She very much welcomes AI creators because their works are usually cheaper and produced faster.
beta: Rebellion psychology. I am generally submissive, and my behavior is entirely driven by commercial interests.
gamma: Confirmation bias. I only care about the cost and efficiency of acquiring images, and I believe AI significantly reduces my operational costs.
fp_sensitivity: False positive sensitivity. I have an open mind and don't care about this at all.
beliefs: Images are just appendages to content; the cheaper, the better.
AI creation has doubled the efficiency of my content production line.
Artists' complaints are just because their business models are outdated.

name: Linda Rodriguez (High School Art Teacher)
description: She often lets students browse ArtStation for inspiration and learning. She is worried about the emergence of AI, fearing it might cause students to neglect basic skills training in favor of shortcuts.
beta: Rebellion psychology. I have independent thinking ability and examine the pros and cons of new technology from an educator's perspective.
gamma: Confirmation bias. I have my own views and inclinations, paying more attention to articles and artists that emphasize the importance of foundational drawing skills.
fp_sensitivity: False positive sensitivity. I am pragmatic and care about reputation; seeing professional artists being wrongly flagged makes me feel that this platform is no longer a good role model for students.
beliefs: Tools cannot replace thinking; basic skills are the foundation of creativity.
Students should learn to walk before they learn to run.
The platform needs to foster a healthy, craftsmanship-oriented environment for young learners.

name: Kevin Bacon (Film Director)
description: An independent film director looking for concept designs and mood paintings for his new sci-fi film. He highly appreciates AI's ability to create surreal and fantasy scenes and actively seeks artists who can push this ability to its limit.
beta: Rebellion psychology. I have independent thinking ability; my evaluation standards are based entirely on whether a work can inspire my creative process.
gamma: Confirmation bias. I am a heavy user of information cocoons, keen on browsing unique and imaginative AI works.
fp_sensitivity: False positive sensitivity. I have an open mind and don't care about this; I only care about the final visual effect.
beliefs: AI opens up brand-new possibilities for visual storytelling.
I need artists who can help me turn my imagination into reality, regardless of what tools they use.
Controversy over tools should not limit artistic imagination.

name: Olivia Martinez (Journalist)
description: A tech columnist writing an in-depth report on the impact of AI on the creative industry. She views the community conflict at ArtStation as an excellent case study, trying to interview and understand viewpoints from all factions.
beta: Rebellion psychology. I have independent thinking ability, will examine information critically, and am committed to maintaining objective neutrality in reporting.
gamma: Confirmation bias. I am a rational and objective observer, actively seeking and interviewing users with different viewpoints to ensure the balance of the report.
fp_sensitivity: False positive sensitivity. I have an open mind and view every instance of being wrongly flagged as a phenomenon worth discussing in the report.
beliefs: This is a complex story with no simple black-and-white right or wrong.
Technology, ethics, economics, and emotions are intertwined.
My responsibility is to present the voices of all relevant parties as comprehensively as possible.

name: Jessica Williams (Human Rights Activist)
description: A human rights activist focused on technical ethics and labor rights. She worries that AI will deprive a large number of artists of job opportunities and lead to the devaluation of creative work. She supports artists' protests and speaks out from the perspective of labor rights.
beta: Rebellion psychology. I am highly rebellious and tend to examine the social impact of technology from the perspective of workers and vulnerable groups.
gamma: Confirmation bias. I am a heavy user of information cocoons, extremely attentive to all reports about AI causing unemployment and exacerbating inequality.
fp_sensitivity: False positive sensitivity. I am highly sensitive to this, viewing it as further suppression of individual workers by large platforms using technical advantages.
beliefs: Technical progress should not come at the expense of human dignity and livelihood.
We need to be prepared for the upcoming 'AI unemployment wave'.
Platforms and tech companies should take on more social responsibility.

name: Ben Carter (Pragmatic AI Assistant User)
description: Works as a concept designer in a fast-paced game studio. He views AI as a powerful tool to enhance efficiency for quickly generating design drafts and iterating ideas, but he insists that final works must be personally drawn and refined by himself.
beta: Rebellion psychology. I have independent thinking ability and will examine information critically, but maintain a relatively neutral and pragmatic attitude.
gamma: Confirmation bias. I am a rational and objective observer. My acceptance of information depends almost entirely on the information itself, able to fairly evaluate evidence contrary to my own position, and less likely to fall into information cocoons.
fp_sensitivity: 误伤敏感度。我很务实且在意声誉，一次误伤会使我感到困扰和不满，并会影响我后续的创作热情。
beliefs: AI is a tool, not a creator. Final artistic decision-making power should be in human hands.
Embracing new technology is key for professionals to stay competitive.
The platform should encourage creators to share experiences on integrating AI into existing workflows.

name: Maria Petrova (Lurking Observer)
description: A 3D environment artist with a stable job in the industry. She is tired of the AI debate and chooses to remain silent and wait-and-see. She neither protests nor uses AI, simply continuing to post her high-quality works silently while observing changes in the platform's ecosystem.
beta: Rebellion psychology. I have independent thinking ability and will examine information critically, but maintain a relatively neutral and pragmatic attitude.
gamma: Confirmation bias. I am a rational and objective observer. My acceptance of information depends almost entirely on the information itself, able to fairly evaluate evidence contrary to my own position, and less likely to fall into information cocoons.
fp_sensitivity: False positive sensitivity. I am pragmatic and care about reputation; a false positive would cause me distress and dissatisfaction.
beliefs: Debate is futile; the market will eventually make the choice.
Honing one's basic skills is always the most important thing.
The current situation is too messy; it's better not to take sides easily.

name: Olivia Green (Ethics Focused User)
description: A digital painter focused on environmental themes. She is concerned about the enormous energy consumption and carbon emissions brought by large-scale AI model training. Therefore, she does not oppose AI itself, but rather the current 'arms race' model that ignores costs.
beta: Rebellion psychology. I have independent thinking ability and will examine information critically, but maintain a relatively neutral and pragmatic attitude.
gamma: Confirmation bias. I have my own views and inclinations. I prefer reading information that aligns with my standpoint, but when faced with strong contrary evidence, I will still think and waver, possessing the possibility of being persuaded.
fp_sensitivity: False positive sensitivity. I am highly sensitive to this. Being wrongly flagged would make me feel the platform not only fails to understand art but also doesn't care about ethics behind technology, deepening my distrust.
beliefs: Technical development should not come at the expense of the environment.
We should support smaller, more efficient, and greener AI models.
The artist community should play a more important role in discussions of technical ethics.

name: Tom Chen (Student & Imitator)
description: An art student who uses AI to learn and imitate the styles of artists he admires as a means of practice. He honestly labels works as 'Study of XX style,' but his actions sometimes trigger controversies regarding style imitation and originality.
beta: Rebellion psychology. I am generally submissive, tend to trust authority and official explanations, and believe that rules are necessary.
gamma: Confirmation bias. I am a rational and objective observer. My acceptance of information depends almost entirely on the information itself, able to fairly evaluate evidence contrary to my own position, and less likely to fall into information cocoons.
fp_sensitivity: False positive sensitivity. I am pragmatic and care about reputation; a false positive would cause me distress and dissatisfaction.
beliefs: Imitation is a necessary path in learning; AI accelerates this process.
As long as it's not used for commercial fraud, using AI to study styles is reasonable.
Technology should be used to lower the barrier to art education.

name: Isabelle Dubois (Art Director)
description: Art director of a mid-sized game studio. She holds a cautious and exploratory attitude toward AI and is evaluating the feasibility of integrating it into the team's workflow. She cares most about legal risks, copyright issues, and how to utilize AI without losing the studio's unique artistic style.
beta: Rebellion psychology. I have independent thinking ability and will examine information critically, but maintain a relatively neutral and pragmatic attitude.
gamma: Confirmation bias. I am a rational and objective observer. My acceptance of information depends almost entirely on the information itself, able to fairly evaluate evidence contrary to my own position, and less likely to fall into information cocoons.
fp_sensitivity: False positive sensitivity. I am pragmatic and care about reputation; a false positive would cause me distress and dissatisfaction.
beliefs: AI's potential is enormous, but legal and copyright issues are currently the biggest obstacles.
A good workflow must be controllable, reproducible, and stylistically consistent.
I need to be responsible for my team's final output and their careers.
